I think the minutes disparity of the player rotations in the preseason is better than the regular season Just looking at many of the box scores of the preseason games and I can't help but to think, 'What if there's a rule that no player in the NBA is allowed to exceed 25 minutes in a game?' It would be interesting to see the chess match every game and how and when coaches utilize their best players from a minutes standpoint. For example, do you play your best player in the first 10 minutes of the first quarter, sit them for the rest of the second quarter, play the first 5 minutes of the third, then the last 10 minutes of the fourth? What if your team is down in the second half of the third quarter, do you risk playing your best player(s) to try and get back into the game, but only have them available for a small portion of the fourth? etc etc Love the preseason in this aspect seeing what the nba stars could do in just 15-20 minutes of action.

Is Michael Jordan Even a top 3 player of all time? Honestly, I don’t think Michael Jordan is a top 3 player because a lot of his legacy comes from winning championships and dominating an era that was very different from today’s NBA. The game has evolved a lot since the 1990s, with players becoming more skilled at shooting threes, creating their own shots, and playing in more versatile offensive systems. It is difficult to compare Jordan directly to modern players because he never had to face the same styles of play or level of three-point shooting that players deal with today. Players like LeBron James had to maintain their dominance across different eras, teams, and playing styles, while Shaq and Steph Curry brought completely different strengths to the game. Jordan also played on incredibly well-built Bulls teams with Scottie Pippen and Phil Jackson, which helped him win six championships. I’m not saying Jordan wasn’t an all-time great, because his scoring, defense, and competitiveness were incredible, but I think people sometimes let nostalgia and his legendary status influence their rankings too much. Being the most iconic player doesn’t automatically mean he has to be top 3.
